payload.prompt:
A photorealistic environmental portrait centers on a woman with the reference face and black bob with wispy bangs, beside a small wood fire. Visible flames rise from burning fuel. The supplied photograph guides her facial proportions, black chin-length hair and fine fringe as she appears in a newly staged coastal moment. At dusk on the black-sand shore of a lagoon, a passing squall has left glossy basalt slabs, low grey cloud and wind-driven drizzle. She has stopped above the tide line to heat water, and is holding a curved steel windscreen steady so the kettle can keep boiling. She crouches to the left of a shallow iron brazier, both boot soles planted on a flat basalt slab, her bent knees supporting an easy forward lean. Her navy weather jacket has a rust-colored wool collar, and its wet fabric folds naturally at the elbows. Her right gloved hand grips the cool upper rim of the windscreen on the upwind left side of the brazier; her visible forearm connects that hand to her right elbow. Her other gloved hand rests on her own near thigh. The screen, glove, fire and kettle are all visible with clear space between their edges. Two split logs lie in the brazier, their blackened surfaces split by dull red-orange embers; yellow-orange flame tongues remain attached to the logs and lean toward the right with the wind. The open front of the brazier exposes recognizable wood surfaces beneath the fire, with several continuous flame tongues attached to those surfaces and open gaps between the wood and flame tips. A single irregular charcoal fleck with a dark center and glowing orange edge has lifted from the exposed log end, separated from that fuel by a visible sliver of air. A squat metal kettle stands on a low stable grate directly over the burning wood. Thin grey smoke begins at the charred log ends, while pale translucent steam begins at the kettle spout; their separate origins stay readable as both drift into the damp air. The brazier's firelight warms her fire-facing cheek and the kettle flank, while her far cheek falls into cooler, darker shadow. A small broken orange reflection lies on the wet basalt beside the brazier. She looks down toward the kettle with focused eyes and a faint softening around her mouth, caught at the moment the fragile little boil holds despite the gust. The cold blue-grey lagoon, rippled water and distant black dune ridge stay visible behind her. A camera at her crouching eye level sees her from a front three-quarter position, using a 40mm environmental-portrait perspective with enough depth of field to keep her face, gripping glove, kettle spout, fuel and the nearby wet stone readable in one landscape frame. Real skin texture, wet fabric, restrained highlight roll-off and the fire's localized warm light preserve the feeling of a candid field photograph.
